Meanwhile, EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents explicitly retains a branch for destinations without credentialId, where it calls createEvent for every credential of matching integration type — in that path a destinationCalendar row with null credentialId cannot match `cal.credentialId === credentialId`, so the find returns undefined and the event is written to 'primary' instead of the configured destination calendar's externalId. judged_text: createEvent resolves the target calendar only via `destinationCalendar.find(cal => cal.credentialId === credentialId)`, so a destinationCalendar row with null credentialId — the legacy case createAllCalendarEvents still explicitly serves through its no-credentialId branch — never matches and the write silently degrades to calendarId 'primary'. Users whose configured destination calendar predates credentialId get new events created on their primary Google calendar instead of the selected destination calendar, with no error anywhere.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.createEvent(calEventRaw, credentialId)`, the calendarId is chosen only via `calEventRaw.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.credentialId === credentialId)?.externalId`, falling back to `"primary"` when no match is found (`calendarId: selectedCalendar || "primary"`). In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, the legacy/no-credentialId path still exists (`else { const destinationCalendarCredentials = ...filter(c => c.type === destination.integration) ... createEvent(c, event) }`), but it does not pass any externalId and the destination entries in that branch can have `credentialId` unset. That means `find(...credentialId...)` returns undefined and Google writes to `primary`, i.e., legacy destinationCalendar rows without credentialId will not be honored and will silently create events on the primary calendar.
